title: Site Insights
summary: I built Site Insights to replace manual site-by-site configuration review with cell inventories, mobility and CA / EN-DC relation tables, and configuration comparisons.
problem: Nokia engineers had to manually inspect each eNB / gNB configuration to review settings and plan client updates or removals. Clients also needed current configuration inventories for planning, while engineers needed a way to identify changes between backups.
built: I built a Python pipeline that parses SCF / XML managed objects into typed inventories, resolves source-to-target candidates, and evaluates handover, reselection, redirection, and EN-DC dependencies. The reporting pipeline also integrates LTE and NR FR1 standalone carrier-aggregation analysis.
decision: Classify mobility candidates as OK, PARTIAL, NOT CONFIGURED, BLOCKED, or AMBIGUOUS, retaining reason summaries and source-object references. Treat redirection as carrier-based so multiple cells on one target carrier do not create false ambiguity.
result: Produces client and internal Excel workbooks with cell information, mobility relationships, and CA / EN-DC configuration evidence. Daily backup comparisons identify configuration deltas; daily / weekly reports give clients current inventories for planning and engineers a history of configuration changes for troubleshooting. The documented Windows package runs without a separate Python installation or runtime internet connection.
limit: Configuration eligibility is evidence about the configured network, not proof that a handover succeeds over the air. Customer configurations and outputs are excluded from this portfolio.
impact: Used internally at Nokia with Apple’s wireless team in Cupertino, Sunnyvale, and Munich. Daily / weekly configuration reports reduce manual preparation for client planning; backup comparisons support Nokia engineers in troubleshooting misconfigurations and tracking daily changes.
details: Problem

Nokia engineers had to manually inspect each eNB / gNB configuration to review settings and plan client updates or removals. Clients also needed current configuration inventories for planning, while engineers needed a way to identify changes between backups.
My ownership
I independently designed and implemented the configuration-analysis and comparison tool to replace manual site-by-site inspection.
Implementation

I built a Python pipeline that parses SCF / XML managed objects into typed inventories, resolves source-to-target candidates, and evaluates handover, reselection, redirection, and EN-DC dependencies. The reporting pipeline also integrates LTE and NR FR1 standalone carrier-aggregation analysis.
Design decisions

Classify mobility candidates as OK, PARTIAL, NOT CONFIGURED, BLOCKED, or AMBIGUOUS, retaining reason summaries and source-object references. Treat redirection as carrier-based so multiple cells on one target carrier do not create false ambiguity.
Verification

The existing 99-test suite passed on an isolated copy during this portfolio review. Synthetic fixtures exercise missing measurement objects, disabled features, ambiguous targets, EN-DC dependencies, workbook generation, and XML / Excel comparisons.
Operational workflow

The tool is used in a daily configuration-backup workflow. Comparing XML snapshots or generated inventories reveals added, removed, and changed configurations. Daily / weekly reports let clients plan from current configurations and help engineers review changes alongside troubleshooting.
Output

A concise client workbook presents configuration inventories and relations; a detailed internal workbook retains dependency decisions and parameter-level troubleshooting. The documented offline Windows package supports environments without a separate Python installation or runtime internet connection.

title: Extended Cellular Analyzer (ECA)
role: Solution architect & team lead · F2G Solutions
summary: I architected ECA around collection, conversion, analysis, and reporting to support test teams with limited access to licensed cellular diagnostic tools.
details: Problem

Test engineers do not always have access to QXDM, TEMS, XCAL, or Shannon licenses. I organized ECA around four recurring needs: collecting captures, converting them, analyzing signaling, and reporting results.
My ownership
I architected the solution and led its development within my team. My implementation contributions include new event parsers and custom .qdss decoding logic.
Collection

I studied open-source parsers to understand Qualcomm baseband packets arriving through the DIAG port, including the 0x7E frame delimiter. Collection uses Qualcomm drivers to extract raw bytes; I extended the available parsing logic with new event parsers.
Conversion
I combined existing open-source conversion logic with custom .qdss decoding logic.
Analysis & reporting
The application brings together live device capture, offline PCAP analysis, GPS mapping, message-level protocol inspection, and CSV / Excel exports.
limit: The public overview describes Windows support and one connected device at a time; simultaneous multi-device capture is planned.

visual.caption: Live signaling capture with message-level protocol inspection.

impact: Supports Nokia drive-test engagements across the Middle East and Africa, particularly Ethiopia, with a collection-to-reporting workflow for teams whose access to commercial diagnostic licenses is not always guaranteed.

title: DTLog
summary: I designed and implemented DTLog end to end to analyze multiple drive-test captures and calculate campaign KPIs and success rates from procedure counters.
problem: Field and network-performance teams need KPI feedback while still at the drive-test site. Sending dozens of large captures to an R&D location delays analysis. Repeated messages and incomplete procedures also make raw message counts unreliable.
built: I designed and implemented the capture-ingestion workflow, decoder and procedure-analysis engine, FastAPI / React dashboard, and Excel reporting. The engine uses retransmission deduplication, state-machine detection, and decoded cause codes.
decision: Give each signaling event one procedure owner. Pool KPI numerators and denominators before calculating rates. Keep indeterminate outcomes separate from observed failures, and show counts when samples are too small for a useful percentage.
result: Provides campaign-level KPI feedback at the drive-test site and connects findings to individual procedures and their evidence. Decode caching supports repeated analysis without dissecting the same capture again.
limit: NR frames can be decoded, but NR procedure segmentation is not implemented. Missing radio metrics are reported as unavailable rather than estimated. Source and capture sets are private.
access: Private repository · case study available here
impact: Gives field-test and network-performance teams KPI feedback at the drive-test site without first transferring dozens of large captures to R&D for analysis. Used in Nokia engagements across the Middle East and Africa, particularly Ethiopia.

title: MOBIQ
role: ADB framework developer & team lead · F2G Solutions
summary: I built MOBIQ’s ADB command foundation to make log-collection campaigns repeatable. My team added a drag-and-drop interface and reusable workflow modules.
details: Problem

Manual attach / detach, calls, SMS, and browsing actions introduce operator variability and human error during log-collection campaigns. Teams need repeatable test sequences without writing device commands for every campaign.
My ownership
I established the ADB automation framework by finding, curating, and organizing commands for attach / detach, calls, SMS, and browsing. These commands became the foundation for reusable test actions.
Team contribution
After I built the command foundation, my team developed the GUI and workflow modules. Test teams assemble actions in a simple drag-and-drop format without creating new commands for each workflow.
Use & scale
Up to six UEs were tested simultaneously. The framework is also used to run repeatable overnight soak-test workflows.
Project scope
Reusable device actions, RF logging, multi-device orchestration, execution retries, and report exports support log-collection campaigns.
limit: Requires Android devices connected through ADB. Campaign execution depends on device connectivity and the configured test modules.

visual.caption: Reusable workflows combine device actions into repeatable test sequences.

impact: Tested with up to six UEs simultaneously and used for overnight soak tests. Repeatable workflows reduce manual actions and operator variability during log collection. Used in Nokia drive-test engagements across the Middle East and Africa, particularly Ethiopia.

title: ECA Mobile
summary: Collect LTE and NR radio measurements on Android, map drive-test routes, and run connectivity and throughput probes in the field.
details: Role
I led this project within my team. Development started in October 2025 and continued in 2026.
Project scope
Live RF values, neighbor-cell information, route logging, ping and throughput tests, Samsung modem-log import, and session exports.
Implementation

The application uses Android telephony APIs to collect available RSRP, RSRQ, SINR, PCI, cell identity, and frequency information alongside GPS location. Foreground-service logging supports measurement collection with the screen off.
limit: Device-exposed LTE/NR metrics depend on the handset and Android version. Continuous GPS and measurement logging increase battery use.

title: LTE KPI clustering
summary: Apply K-means to LTE RSRP, RSRQ, and throughput data to identify heterogeneous coverage regions and cell-edge performance gaps.
problem: A network-wide average can hide local coverage and performance differences. Measurement groups can help reveal regions that deserve a closer RF investigation.
built: I applied K-means clustering to LTE signal and throughput measurements and visualized the resulting coverage regions. The repository includes the notebook, Python implementation, and cluster-map outputs.
decision: Use clustering as an exploratory tool. Interpret clusters against the underlying radio measurements rather than treating a cluster label as a network fault diagnosis.
result: Identified coverage and cell-edge performance gaps and used them to recommend parameter changes in a proof of concept.
limit: This is an exploratory proof of concept. Its findings depend on the dataset and feature selection and should be validated through additional measurements before deployment.

title: CNN QAM denoiser
summary: Investigate convolutional neural networks for denoising QAM-modulated audio signals, connecting signal-processing concepts with machine learning.
problem: Noise degrades communication signals. This project explores whether a learned denoising approach can help recover information from QAM-modulated audio.
built: I explored a convolutional neural network approach to QAM signal denoising. The public repository documents the project as a deep-learning investigation into communication clarity.
decision: Frame learned denoising as an experiment whose value depends on evaluation across noise conditions and against conventional baselines.
result: A research project at the intersection of communications and machine learning, complementing my later work on measurement and validation tools.
limit: The public project summary does not establish a production deployment or a quantified performance advantage. No benchmark result is claimed here.
